title: Boundary-Phase Control of Sequentially Addressed Trapped-Ion ZZ Interactions
authors: Chun-Yang Luan, Haiyu Ding, Cheng-Kang Pan, Xiangjie Li, Lin Cheng, Gangxi Wang, Yuting Lei, Peilin Zheng, Shixin Hu, Xiang Zhang, Fei Wang
abstract: Motion-mediated trapped-ion gates typically apply synchronized state-dependent forces to both target ions. We consider the complementary setting in which one addressing channel alternates between the targets, so their force windows do not overlap. In a complex-amplitude near-resonant description, each window generates a displacement vector, and ordered symplectic products of vectors on different ions produce the ZZ phase. For fixed envelopes and timings, relative rotations of the window displacement vectors redirect the sign and magnitude of this phase, whereas a common rotation of all displacement vectors leaves the pair phase invariant. Motivated by experimental alternating-addressing protocols, we design matched-envelope phase and contrast controls that distinguish the boundary-phase response from closure error and residual force in dark gaps. Waveform synthesis suppresses differential motion, while a reduced-spin map that is exact within the linear spin-dependent-force model accounts for projector-common motion, deterministic local-Z phases, spectator coupling, and control-parameter drift. A conditional-Ramsey protocol predicts continuous and reset contrasts of 0.998 and 0.996, with the reset rule redirecting the extracted pair phase by 0.581 rad relative to the continuous rule, modulo pi/2. In the representative comparison, sequential control uses only one active target channel at a time, but requires 1.826 times the normalized squared-force action of independently calibrated simultaneous control. For representative experimental parameters and within the stated approximations, the inter-window force-quadrature reference therefore provides an experimentally testable control resource for sequential trapped-ion interactions.
summary: The paper develops advanced theoretical protocols to precisely control two-qubit ZZ interactions in trapped ions using alternating addressing channels. By designing matched-envelope controls, the authors successfully isolate the desired boundary-phase response from common experimental errors like closure error. The key finding is that while sequential addressing offers a distinct control mechanism, it incurs a higher resource cost (force action) than simultaneous methods unless channel concurrency is severely limited.
main_problem: The paper addresses how to control two-qubit ZZ interactions in trapped ions when using sequentially addressed force windows, specifically designing controls that isolate the boundary-phase response from experimental errors.
main_result: Sequential addressing can provide an experimentally testable control resource for inter-window phase generation, although it requires a significantly higher normalized squared-force action compared to simultaneous addressing schemes.
method: The authors use matched-envelope conditional-Ramsey protocols and analyze the ordered symplectic product of displacement vectors derived from a near-resonant Hamiltonian description.
model_or_system: The system is trapped ions interacting via motion-mediated gates, modeled using a linear spin-dependent-force Hamiltonian within the Rotating-Wave Approximation (RWA). The dynamics are analyzed by calculating pair phases ($\Phi_{ij}$) from ordered symplectic products of displacement vectors.
key_observables: Pair phase ($\Phi_{ij}$), conditional contrast ($C_{	ext{cond}}$), motional closure error ($D_{ij}$), and the required normalized squared-force action for different addressing schemes.
important_parameters: The relative phase between successive windows, which acts as an independent control coordinate; the ratio of force actions between sequential vs. simultaneous control (e.g., 1.826 times).
main_assumptions: Calculations rely on the linear RWA Hamiltonian and assume ideal dark gaps where external forces are zero; the results are model-based predictions.
figures_summary: Figures compare phase rules affecting raw ZZ phase versus conditional contrast, illustrate symplectic window geometry errors, summarize optimized waveforms showing reduced motional closure, and detail resource trade-offs between sequential and simultaneous control.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical framework for calculating pair phases using ordered symplectic products for nonoverlapping windows. It then introduces matched-envelope protocols to separate phase generation from contrast loss. Finally, it compares the resource costs (force action vs. channel concurrency) of sequential versus simultaneous addressing schemes.
why_interesting: This work provides detailed, quantitative guidelines on optimizing gate sequences in trapped ions by rigorously separating coherent phase control from motional error sources, which is crucial for scaling up quantum computation using ion traps.
